Hi team — summary of current platform defaults for hosted API (customer-managed region, unless otherwise configured):

- Raw request payloads (full request bodies, minus obvious transient debugging headers): retained 30 days by default; metadata index kept for 90 days for billing/usage analytics.
- Model-generated outputs (complete generated text, images, or structured responses): retained 90 days by default for debugging, quality monitoring, and evals. Outputs are included in audit logs for 90 days.
- Prompt templates / customer-supplied prompt metadata (things saved in Console as templates or instruct sets): retained 365 days by default; customers can drop or export these at any time.
- KV cache / session artifacts (in-memory caches, intermediate KV used for streaming): ephemeral — tombstoned after 7 days and removed from active nodes; not replicated to long-term stores.
- Embeddings and vector artifacts: by default retained 90 days; for Hosted customers we offer an opt-out where vectors are not retained beyond immediate compute.

Residency notes: storage is provisioned in the region selected for the account; ephemeral caches may touch compute nodes within additional zones for performance but persistent stores (objects/DB) remain in the account region. For EU-account customers we keep all persistent stores in EU regions unless the customer explicitly requests multi-region backups.

Deletion and export: customers can trigger a delete/export via the Console or API. Deletion pipeline: once an account-initiated deletion request is accepted, persistent artifacts are removed within 24–72 hours; tombstoned entries (e.g., KV cache markers) can take up to 10 days to fully purge from backups depending on the snapshot window.

Dedicated / Private: Dedicated customers can configure retention windows shorter or longer (contracted); Private (on-prem) customers control retention entirely.

Compliance caveats: for SOC2/PCI customers we recommend contractual language to cap default windows (if needed) and to document any allowed longer debugging windows. Also recommend a Data Processing Addendum that clearly enumerates default windows and deletion SLAs.

I attached the platform retention summary and the SOC2 evidence checklist for reference. Happy to convert this into a small matrix for Northstar.

—Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify default retention for requests/outputs (Northstar PII scope)

Alex — thanks for the patience. Below is a concise, customer-ready summary you can use in the RFP/SOC pack. If you need formal language for the DPA or SOW, we can provide that next.

Default retention summary (Hosted accounts) — Redwood Inference
- Raw requests (payloads): 30 days default. Indexed metadata used for billing and routing kept up to 90 days.
- Generated outputs (responses, structured outputs): 90 days default for debugging and quality monitoring.
- Prompt templates / saved prompt metadata: 365 days default; can be deleted/exported anytime.
- KV cache / session artifacts: ephemeral, tombstoned after 7 days; not stored in long-term object stores.
- Embeddings / vector artifacts: 90 days default; opt-out available for Hosted customers who cannot retain vectors.

Residency: persistent stores are kept in the account region by default (EU accounts => EU persistent stores). Short-lived compute caches may be used in adjacent zones for performance; nothing persistent is written outside the selected region unless explicitly enabled.

Deletion SLA: customer-initiated purge of persistent artifacts completes in 24–72 hours; final purge from backups/snapshots can take up to 10 days.

Options for stricter controls:
- Enterprise customers (Dedicated): configurable retention windows via contract and Console settings.
- Private deployments: customer-managed retention entirely.
- Immediate opt-out for embeddings: enable via support request; we set vectors to non-persistent mode.

Next steps:
1) If you want shorter default windows for Northstar, tell us the desired windows and we’ll propose DPA language.
2) I’ve attached the retention matrix and SOC2 evidence checklist for your team.

If Legal Ops wants a one-pager for the SOC packet, Kimberly can produce a redacted snippet.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: retention-matrix-v1.pdf] [Attachment: soc2-evidence-list.pdf]
